notes.title: 24th of November, 2023 - Patch 1.04

- Patched up some seams in the station that were exposed to deep space.

Thanks again for your continued support and patience!
- Conor

notes.title: 9th of November, 2023 - Patch 1.02
notes.content:
Hi there everyone, today we're publishing the 2nd patch for Project Regolith, addressing a number of missing colliders, some issues with world-space portals, a missing achievement trigger, and some other things! Check out our full patch notes below:

[u][b]Project Regolith Update, 9th of November, 2023 - Patch 1.02[/b][/u]
- Fixed a massive performance issue being caused by a check that should've only been run once on the Main Menu. Framerates should be a little more stable on all machines now.

- Made some adjustments to the player's cameras to (hopefully) reduce noticeable clipping through world-space portals.

- Fixed an issue that was preventing an achievement related to [spoiler]the Atrium doors opening, revealing Cronus X[/spoiler] from firing.

- Restored a missing label from the players' settings menus for Caption Opacity. This was previously labelled correctly on the main menu but not during gameplay.

- Fixed an issue that was causing some specific Puzzle-related objects, such as the [spoiler]"Unstable" Model Car in the Admin Puzzle[/spoiler] being respawned in the wrong place when using the "Respawn Objects" pause menu button.

- Updated a few interaction prompts that were displaying the default placeholder "Interact With This Thing" text to display the correct prompt instead.

- Updated some of the prompts on the [spoiler]Terraforming Puzzle's interactable terminals[/spoiler] to better reflect some components that can be interacted with.

- Fixed a number of missing collision issues.

- Fixed some world-space portals being culled/not rendering at incorrect times.

- Fixed the Key Rebinding Settings tab in the Main Menu not displaying the unchangeable bindings for "Display Directive", "Open Codex", and "Text Chat".

- Fixed the End Credits UI being displayed smaller than intended.

- Fixed a missing sound cue on the [spoiler]Atrium Viewing Shutter[/spoiler], more door-related missing SFX fixes will be coming with next week's patch!

----------------------------------------------------------------------

That's all for this week - We're aiming to have another patch next week addressing some more noticeable world-space portal culling, as well as some general level culling/pop-in and out issues with the map.

Thanks for your patience,
- Conor and the Regolith Team

notes.title: Project Regolith - Patch 1.01, 3rd of November, 2023
notes.content:
Hi there folks, we've pushed Project Regolith's first bug-fix patch, aiming at addressing some of the known issues we've spotted since launch a couple of days ago.

3rd of November, 2023 - Patch 1.01:
- Fixed the final puzzle's music cues overlapping the closing music in the game's end sequence.
- Fixed the controls responsible for [spoiler]scuttling the station[/spoiler] not correctly triggering a music cue.
- Moved Crew Log #11 (AKA [spoiler]Nerd Rage[/spoiler]) out of it's confinement near the [spoiler]Terraforming Labs[/spoiler].
- Fixed broken material on the [spoiler]Terraforming Test Tube[/spoiler]'s [spoiler]refined quantum energy[/spoiler] seen during the [spoiler]Terraforming Lab[/spoiler] puzzle.
- Removed an oversized trigger in [spoiler]Terraforming[/spoiler] that was causing LightBot to teleport somewhere he shouldn't, softlocking the game.
- Implemented a fix for rare cases of the [spoiler]Station Control Arming Keys[/spoiler] not spawning correctly during the [spoiler]Admin[/spoiler] puzzle.
- (Hopefully) Fixed an issue with loading the game from some checkpoints immediately crashing the host out of the scene. If you have any issues loading from checkpoints, please submit a bug report either in-game or via our Discord!
- Attempting a fix for some players having their FPS locked to 20 - Not 100% certain that this will work, so if you're feeling like your framerate is locked in-game to a low value, please report it in our Discord or in the Steam Discussions!

notes.title: Devlog #19 - PAX Prep, Glow-ups, We're on TikTok Now (finally)
notes.content:
[h3]Hey everyone, it's time for another devlog. [/h3]

In our last update we went over just how busy October is for us.
Between all the events and finalizing things on the game, this post is gonna be a bit brief once again, but we wanted to go over our final prep for PAX Aus, show off the glow-up that the game's main menu received, and also announce that we've (finally) started posting content on TikTok!
[h2]
PAX Preparation[/h2]
It's no secret that we've put a lot of our eggs in the events basket for Project Regolith, with SXSW Sydney, the Steam Next-Fest, and of course, PAX Aus all coming up, one after the other, right before launch. We've spent a decent chunk of time making sure that the demo we'll be bringing works well, and gets the main idea of the game across to everyone who visits.

On top of that, we've got some extra goodies for the booth, too! [b]The first 50 teams to complete the demo each day[/b] get to take home a pair of these incredible, official Project Regolith pins! 

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/43307026/4ac393edeb9aca5d6b50bcef75f975183c64780f.jpg[/img]
[h2]
Glow-ups[/h2]
Speaking of Demo prep, something that's long needed some attention was the game's UI. We've been running with the same old, dated menu screen since the middle of last year, and the same Player UI layout since even earlier, way back in pre-Alpha. Given they're some of the first things a new Player sees, it's definitely something that we wanted to improve on. And we think we've managed to do it with this new UI setup:

[code][img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/43307026/43b7ab7557859457559677cd0f200afa08d2cb94.png[/img]
                                    [i] The boring, lame, old Main Menu UI [/i]

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/43307026/4670b623be3ec89d236b6a5ed47c3ec1e294400e.png[/img]
                                    [i]The sleek, new, AMAZING Main Menu UI[/i][/code]

We're still sorting out a nice background for the Main Menu, but for now, just the layout in general is MUCH more pleasing to the eye.

But it's not just the main menu that's been given some love:

[code][img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/43307026/c9898772d87474c32de0f6c2e032a03b246f5a22.png[/img]
                                      [i]Old, busted, Pre-Alpha Player UI[/i]

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/43307026/ce8df72aa6809b787801e4c81fb5d6e37010d20b.png[/img]
                                      [i]The new, prettier Player UI[/i][/code]
UI isn't a strong-suit on the team, but we're all a lot happier with the new layouts we have!


[h2]TikTok Time?[/h2]
Lastly, you read it right - After months of saying "Content Soon" and even being dropped from our social links, [b]the Regolith TikTok FINALLY HAS CONTENT![/b] It's about time, I know. [url=https://www.tiktok.com/@regolith_interactive]You can follow us here![/url] And while you're at it, check out all our other socials outlined at the end of the post.


[h2]See you at PAX AUS![/h2]
And with that, this update draws to a close. If your'e attending PAX AUS this weekend, make sure to stop by the booth, [b]Booth 11 at PAX RISING![/b]

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/43307026/e1e8171fdcfce2a2c6366751e992fc139bdae1e5.png[/img]

These Steam Devlogs will be going weekly from now till the launch of the game, as we cover the final journey to release and the myriad of events occuring this month. 
Tune in next week for lots of lovely pictures and stories from PAX and news regarding the Steam Next Fest! or follow our socials for regular updates.

'Till next time, take care!

notes.title: Public Devlog #13: Gold Milestone and Launch Window
notes.content:
[h3]Hello once again everyone, and welcome to this very special development update![/h3]

[url=https://store.steampowered.com/news/app/2220420/view/3671044735536723893]Last update we outlined how the project had shaped up during Beta.[/url] This week we'll be talking about our final Milestone coming up in the next few months, the Gold Milestone. We'd also like to spend a bit of time talking about our plans for Marketing, and the final launch window for Project Regolith. So without further ado, let's get right down to it...

[h2]The Gold Milestone[/h2]
As our final production milestone leading up to launch, our approach to Gold can be summed up broadly by the phrase "Get the game finished", but of course, there's a lot of work that's going to go into it, so let's talk details:

[b]Puzzles and Environments[/b] - It should come as no surprise that making sure all our environments are up-to-scratch in our main puzzle areas is a top priority for the team. While we mentioned last update that all our puzzles are in a playable state in a vacuum, there's still a ways to go in terms of environmental storytelling and environmental cues that help provide context or hints to certain puzzles narrative-wise. And that will be a major part of our focus throughout Gold.

[b]Narrative[/b] - Somewhat tying in to environmental work is our Narrative elements. As we've made a point of discussing in our updates, we've got a whole slew of Voice Actors whose work we've been receiving, reviewing, and preparing to implement into the game. The crew members of Outpost Rhea have their voices, and making sure they're heard in the right place and at the right time is something we're talking about. You'll also be able to revisit logs you've previously found, review transcripts, and read additional lore entries in our in-game Codex!

[b]Polish and Testing[/b] - I mentioned in our last update that external testing wasn't something we'd had much time for during Beta, and we're definitely aiming to remedy that as we push through the next few months. We're currently planning out when, where, and how we intend to get the game tested, and we'll hopefully talk a bit more about it in a future post.

Once we've got some solid, actionable data from our testers, we'll get to work on sanding down rough edges, fixing as many bugs as we can leading to launch, and overall making the game experience better!


[h2]Marketing[/h2]
As you might've guessed, marketing an Indie title is no small feat. We've been steadily growing our following on social media the past few months, but not at a pace we're particularly pleased with. Unfortunately, being a small team of 4 limits the amount of time we can spend engaging on Socials without taking time away from the actual production. We've been looking into other means of promotion for Project Regolith, and we've come up with a few ideas:

[b]Social Media Goals/Calls to Action[/b] - To try help drive engagement on our socials we've started setting incremental goals for each avenue. The first of which has been our effort to hit 200 Followers on our Twitter with a payoff of unlocking the 2nd Track from our OST (speaking of which, don't forget to check out the teaser below and subscribe to our YouTube!)

[previewyoutube=dlAHag757z0;full][/previewyoutube]

[b]Upcoming Events[/b] - Some of you may remember seeing us at PAX Australia 2022 last year, and showcasing our progress again this year is definitely something we want to leave on the table. Not only that, but we've also been considering South By Southwest Sydney (SXSW) as a candidate for promoting Project Regolith here in Australia. While nothing's set in stone just yet, we'll be sure to keep you all posted on events we'll be attending!

[b]The Steam Next-Fest (October 2023 Edition)[/b] - If you've been on Steam the past couple of weeks you no doubt noticed the June edition of the Steam Next-Fest, a showcase of upcoming Indie titles, livestreams, and playable Demos. This October the Next-Fest is returning once again, and we're intending to participate with Project Regolith, and a refurbished/relaunched version of our Hydroponics demo, with all of it's final assets in place.

Unfortunately, this has fairly important implications on our launch window, as titles that participate in the Next-Fest [b]can't[/b] be already released.


[h2]Launch Window[/h2]
So what does this mean for launch? Well, ultimately we're aiming to keep our deadlines the same, with the game being done by late-August, and leaving us with some wiggle-room for all the things we've outlined above. But in order to participate, we'll have to push back our planned launch-window by a little bit.

After a lengthy discussion amongst the team, we've decided that it would be silly to pass up an opportunity to help push the game to as many eyes as possible leading up to launch, and we've decided that this small delay is necessary. (It also moves us away from the launch windows of some much larger AAA Sci-Fi titles in late August/early September)

For this delay, we'd like to apologize. We hope you all understand the reasoning behind our decision. But we'd like to officially declare...

[h3][b][u]Project Regolith will release this October, following the conclusion of the Steam Next-Fest![/u][/b][/h3]

We'll leave you with that exciting bit of news for this week's update. Stay tuned for more information over the next few weeks! 

- Ryan

notes.title: Public Devlog #12: Beta Wrap Up
notes.content:
[h3]Hello, and welcome to our final steam update for the Beta milestone![/h3]

In case you missed it, [url=https://store.steampowered.com/news/app/2220420/view/3666539867375104525?l=english]a couple of weeks [/url]ago we talked a bit about the sounds behind Outpost Rhea, showed off 'The Hydroponics Lab' track from the game's OST, and teased a new track, '"Routine" Maintenance' to be released once we reach 200 Twitter followers:

[previewyoutube=dlAHag757z0;full][/previewyoutube]
Be sure to follow us on [url=https://twitter.com/Regolith_Int]Twitter[/url], if you haven't already, if you wanna hear the full track.

[h2]Beta Progress[/h2]
The past couple of months of updates have been heavily focused on SFX, Music, and Voice Acting. With Gold milestone fast approaching, we figured it's long overdue to talk again about progress on the actual game. Back in early April, we discussed our Journey Into Beta, and outlined a series of goals:

[list]
[*] [b]Major Puzzles[/b] connected by spaces that are sufficiently detailed and make reasonable in-universe sense to be there. 
[*] [b]Critical bugs are minimized[/b] to reduce programming workload leading to launch. 
[*][b] VA Casting completed for all Major and Minor roles[/b], with Major roles recorded and pending any required script changes/re-recordings. 
[*] [b]Player and Puzzle-specific SFX recorded[/b], most ambient and other non-priority sounds pending. 
[*] [b]Testing data on puzzle difficulty and readability[/b] ready to inform possible changes. 
[/list]
With our internal deadline for Beta coming up, now seems like a perfect time to talk about these goals, and how the team feels we're progressing towards them.

[h3]Music, SFX, and VA Casting and Recording [/h3]
We've spoken at length about our sounds the past few updates, so to keep it brief here - We're pretty happy with our progress on this front. - Not only is our entire VA Cast decided, we've also had the game's OST in the final stages of production with Simon, as well as a varied range of SFX coming in for specific puzzle and environmental elements aboard the station.

[h3]Puzzle Functionality [/h3]
As Beta has progressed the past few months, we've made a concentrated effort on puzzle functionality. As it stands today, each of our major puzzles is playable and solvable within a vacuum. You're probably asking "What does that actually mean?" though.

Let's say we were to drop you into one of our puzzles as it is right now, with ZERO context, ZERO clues, and ZERO guidance. Just you and a bunch of random puzzle elements. Given enough time, you'd probably be able to work out specifics and complete the puzzle, but it'd take a lot longer than what we'd like for the final product, and you probably wouldn't have too much fun with the guesswork.

At the end of the day, the puzzles are "solvable", but are missing a lot of quality-of-life and narrative features that'll make them launch-ready. As we continue to get our VA Audio implemented in-engine, the gap between now and Gold will steadily close.

[h3]Bug Fixes[/h3] 
As you might come to expect in any software field, bug fixing is a steady and ongoing task. But on the programming side, we're feeling pretty good about the state of things. Since our patch to the demo at the end of March this year we haven't encountered any serious issues with Networking, and despite the occasional small issue popping up in testing, things are looking and feeling good. Although, speaking of testing...

[h3]Testing Data[/h3]
We've been discussing how best to tackle a few elements of testing, particularly focused on "Fun" testing - Making sure the puzzles as they are right now are fun to play and solve. - Admittedly, we haven't had much opportunity to see the puzzles played by third-parties so far. Something we're aiming to remedy as we move towards Launch.

Originally we had planned to have some testing data before the end of Beta production, however, this hasn't really panned out as we'd hoped. For now, the goal posts have been moved back for testing into early Gold production, which will be running from July through to the end of August.

And lastly, you may have noticed I'd neglected to mention the first goal: Connecting the Major Puzzles together...


[h2]Environment Glow-ups[/h2]
A major part of our environmental workflow in Project Regolith is modular pieces. Not only because it makes building areas simpler, but it also makes sense that deep-space construction would be done using modular materials. One of our major concerns though, was that a lot of the station may end up looking too similar and areas we wanted to stand out more would blend together with others.

Our solution for this was to adjust the workflow slightly, and also split our pieces into a couple of categories - One that fits the more sterile and industrial elements of the station, such as the Engineering department or Maintenance areas - And another that feels a little more livable, suited for more "Civilian" aspects of the station.

In a couple of rarer cases, we've also got more purpose-built areas that don't fit this modular mold perfectly... But we'll save those for another update.

For now - Here's a peek at this workflow in action with some work-in-progress lighting with the Hydroponics puzzle found in the Steam Demo:

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/43307026/4fec0422a4d224b560b1a37b1f086fc6065437fd.gif[/img]

Ultimately, we're a lot happier with the cleaner style of the new area. We're excited to share some more progress shots of the space as the lighting is improved and we move closer to launch. And if you preferred the older look, not to worry, plenty of other areas will be maintaining that more industrial modular style!

And with that, today's update comes to a close and so does the Beta milestone! Next time we'll be talking a bit more about our goals lfor the Gold milestone, and what that'll mean for the project! 'Til then, you can get more updates and content on our socials!

notes.title: Public Devlog #07 - Journey Into Beta
notes.content:
[h2]Hello folks, happy belated Easter![/h2]

This week's update aims to give a bit of an outline of our next major milestone - Beta, and the direction we'll be taking with the game for the next couple of months.

[h2]State of the Game[/h2]
As I mentioned in our post a couple of weeks ago, we're now officially past our Alpha milestone with all our major puzzles base functionality ready and pending some additional art and QoL passes coming up.

During Beta, our aim is to get each of these areas playable in a single contiguous experience, and to expose the puzzles we've not yet shown off to some testing audiences (more on that in a future update!) to help give us an idea on adjustments we'll need to make, or important bugs we'll need to iron out in the lead-up to our Gold milestone later in the year.

So, with that said, the most important details for us in the coming weeks include building the areas of the station that connect our major puzzles together, testing for issues in our current puzzles, continuing casting for VA's as outlined last update, and lastly, improving the overall soundscape of Outpost Rhea.

[h2]To summarize our criteria for Beta:[/h2]

[b]Major Puzzles [/b]connected by spaces that are sufficiently detailed and make reasonable in-universe sense to be there.
[b]Critical bugs[/b] are minimized to reduce programming workload leading to launch.
[b]VA Casting[/b] completed for all Major and Minor roles, with Major roles recorded and pending any required script changes/re-recordings.
[b]Player and Puzzle-specific SFX[/b] recorded, most ambient and other non-priority sounds pending.
[b]Testing data[/b] on puzzle difficulty and readability ready to inform possible changes.
We're more than happy to go into a little more detail on any of these points in our official Discord, so if you've got any questions feel free to ask us there! (Or in the comments on this post, too!)

That's all for now, as always we'll keep you guys up-to-date on any important developments - 'till next time though, here's a quick sneak-peek at a before/after update Brandon's been working on for the Hydroponics Bay's plant life.

notes.title: Public Devlog #06 - The End of Alpha
notes.content:
[h2]Hello again everyone!
[/h2]
Development is in full swing here at the new office with the Alpha build of the game drawing to a close. What a busy few weeks we've had since our last update, allow me to let you in on what's been going on here at Regolith.


[h2]VA Casting Process[/h2]
If you read out last update, two weeks ago we put out an open casting call to several Voice Acting communities, as well as on our social media platforms - Since then, we've received a more than a whopping 300+ auditions. This response has been incredible and starting this week we've begun to review them all to find our future Outpost Rhea Crew! To give you all a more concrete timeline on how we're planning to tackle this task, here's our upcoming deadlines for VA work.

[strike][b]Monday, 20th of March[/b] - Open casting call within VA Communities, Social Networks.[/strike]

[b]Monday, 3rd of April[/b] - Audition submissions closed, review for roles and callback selection process.
[i]We are now here![/i]

[b]Monday, 17th of April[/b] - Callback talent approached, final casting process with more thorough auditions.

[b]Monday, 1st of May [/b]- Final cast decided, official recording process begins.

We're really excited to progress further with bringing the story behind Outpost Rhea and its crew to life, and this is the first big step towards being able to tell the narrative we want to tell across the station.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/43307026/bb2aad1b99f2f17b36ff2e6d06a5e3e933d6a7eb.png[/img]


[h2]Demo Patch[/h2]
Also on the agenda, is to cover a bit more about the small patch we released to the Public Demo this past fortnight. While a relatively small update, this patch fixed a number of small issues involved with connecting to other players via Steamworks servers. Primarily issues that arose during the joining process, and with rehosting lobbies after leaving an active game.

So if you were having any issues playing the demo, now's a great time to check it out again! Don't forget to report any issues you find to us via the official Discord, or using the Steam Discussions pages!


[h2]Progress Update[/h2]
Lastly, I'd like to quickly update you all on general progress on the game since it's been a little while since our last detailed check-in. Things have been progressing smoothly, albeit with a couple of hitches here and there.

While we had to push back our plans for Alpha by a month due to the issues with getting into our new office, we're now back on track for the most part since settling into the space. In our initial outline of expectations for Alpha, we mentioned wanting all major puzzles being playable within a vacuum, which we're super close to, the main OST of the game has been put together (by the amazing Simon Stemberger!) and is pending setup in FMOD to go into the game, and lastly, as we outlined, we've got the main script of the game ready to go and the VA Casting Process is underway!

So to summarize, we're making solid progress and are still feeling confident as we approach the end of the alpha phase, and there's plenty to be excited about in the upcoming few weeks of development.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/43307026/06c3b197b9a43644deb11572cf917b6e098cf76d.png[/img]

Join us again in a couple of weeks where we'll be outlining our next milestone... Beta!

And as always, don't forget to throw us a follow on the socials or share the game with someone you know:

Cheers,

- Ryan
